analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expresses dissatisfaction about a £12 late payment fee and asks for it to be removed, alleging financial loss (CH-1). They admit the payment was a day late.
analysis.summary: [PERSON_1] was charged a £12 late payment fee on a credit card ending [CARD_DIGITS_1]. They paid by bank transfer on the 15th, one day after the 14th due date, and say they forgot. They report no missed payments in 6 years and ask for the fee to be removed as a one-off. The handler notes this is the first late fee in 12 months, that no vulnerability indicators were seen, and that the customer prefers email. The October 2026 statement is on file.

timeline.event: Credit card payment due date, as stated by the customer
Customer paid by bank transfer, one day after the due date
Complaint received via web form; handler noted first late fee in 12 months, no vulnerability indicators, email preferred

analysis.severity_reason: Financial loss is £12, under £100, with no other CH-6 High or Medium triggers (CH-6).

vulnerability.suggested_support: None identified. Offer support if the customer raises any need.

analysis.routing_reason: No ESC-1 trigger applies: no fraud, lending decision, vulnerability referral, systemic issue or app failure. The complaints handler can resolve this.

policy_citations.quote: A late payment fee on a credit card is correctly charged if the minimum payment was not received by the due date.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The customer admits paying a day after the due date and does not mention a failed Direct Debit, so the fee appears to be correctly charged.

policy_citations.quote: a complaints handler may refund up to two fees of the same type in any rolling 12-month period as a goodwill gesture.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The handler's note says this is the first late fee in 12 months, so the discretionary refund provision is relevant for the handler's decision.

policy_citations.quote: *Low*: financial loss under £100 or a service issue with no loss.
policy_citations.how_it_applies: The £12 fee sets severity as Low.

handover.complaint_summary: Customer was charged a £12 late payment fee on their credit card after paying one day after the due date. They ask for it to be removed as a one-off.
handover.vulnerability_assessment: No vulnerability indicators found (note_1). It is not recorded that the customer was asked about support needs.

analysis.suggested_next_step: The complaints handler should check the statement for the due date and payment receipt date, then decide whether to apply the FEE-3 discretionary refund. The handler should reply by email.
